titleEn: Water from the Eaves—Whoosh, All Clean!

pages.text: Taro had dug in the soil all day. He was muddy all over. Mom filled the yard basin. "Wash before dinner." "I don't like water! It gets in my eyes."
Taro tucked himself into the farthest corner under the eaves. Dry mud rustled on his back. Rain poured outside.
Sitting still, Taro felt itchy and prickly at the back of his neck. He scratched his arms hard. "Why do I feel so uncomfortable?"
When the rain grew lighter, Mumu bounded under the eaves and pointed to their edge. Water gathered on the roof fell in a whooshing stream.
"That's not a basin—it's water coming down from the sky." Taro reached out. The water felt lukewarm and gently washed mud from the back of his hand.
"Stand with your back to it, and the mud washes off by itself!" Mumu stepped under first. Muddy water ran down their back. Eyes closed tight, Mumu called, "Water from the Eaves—Whoosh, All Clean!"
Taro stood in the middle of the stream. Water whooshed down his back. He rubbed his face with his hands and stretched his long tail to rinse it, too. "Water from the Eaves—Whoosh, All Clean!"
His itchy back felt refreshed, and his fur grew smooth. "Water can feel this good?" Mumu pricked up one ear to listen to the rain.
Taro counted on his fingers. "One, put my back under the stream! Two, rub my face with my hands! Three, rinse right to my tail!" Whenever rain grew lighter, Taro ran to the eaves first.

Mom wrapped Taro in dry leaves, hugged him, and patted his back. Feeling fresh after washing made meals and sleep sweeter. He smiled up at the water. "Mumu, let's stand here together again! Water from the Eaves—Whoosh, All Clean!"
